source: Flashlight Emitter Reference — Lumens, CRI, Candela & Throw.md

emitters.name: 519A
emitters.notes_html: The all-round gold standard. Wide range of CCTs (roughly 2700K–5700K), neutral to rosy tint. Floody with the dome on. Easily dedomed for more throw, a lower CCT and a rosier tint. "V1" is the newer, preferred revision (BLF Guide, Emisar).

best_for.why_html: High CRI, easy to drive, great tint

best_for.pick_html: Nichia E21A, 519A or LatticePower CSP2323 in a triple
best_for.why_html: Small, efficient, high CRI at the low currents tiny cells can supply

emitters.name: 219B
emitters.notes_html: Legendary rosy tint (especially the sw45k 4500K bin). Low output and dislikes high current; largely replaced by 519A / NTG35 (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: 219F
emitters.notes_html: Successor to the 219C; best known for an 1800K sodium-lamp-like version. Doesn't like being overdriven (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: B35AM
emitters.notes_html: Four tiny dies with a natural, sunlight-like tint. Its odd footprint needs a dedicated MCPCB, which limits overdrive (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: 719A
emitters.notes_html: Flat (domeless) emitter with two stacked dies. Colour like a dedomed 519A with more output but a floodier beam; generally considered underwhelming (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: 144A
emitters.notes_html: Nichia's answer to the XHP50 (different footprint, no thermal pad). High CRI but strong tint shift without diffusion; used in the Armytek Wizard C2 Pro Nichia (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: E21A / E17A
emitters.notes_html: Ultra-high CRI, usually used in quads or larger arrays. 1850K–6500K, plus specialty colours such as E17A Azure (BLF Guide).

best_for.pick_html: Nichia E21A, 519A or LatticePower CSP2323 in a triple
best_for.why_html: Small, efficient, high CRI at the low currents tiny cells can supply

emitters.name: SFT-25R
emitters.notes_html: Small round die (about half the SFT-40's area) = extreme throw; out-throws the SFT-40 in the same host. Standard 3535 footprint fits most EDC/thrower boards (BLF test, Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Tiny intense hotspot; ~2× W1's lumens, slightly less intensity

best_for.why_html: Tiny domeless die = highest luminance of any LED = most candela per lumen

emitters.name: SFT-40
emitters.notes_html: Domeless all-round thrower king: punchy hotspot with usable spill. 6500K leans green, 5000K is decent, and 3000K is the high-CRI version (BLF Guide, Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Best all-round thrower hotspot (more usable spill than SFT-25R)

best_for.why_html: Best hotspot-to-spill balance
Rosy (FFL) or warm 95 CRI (SFT-40) alternatives to cool-white throwers
Warm CCT cuts back-scatter glare

emitters.name: SFT-70
emitters.notes_html: Domeless SST-70; efficient boost/buck-driven thrower. Convoy lists four bins with CRI from 70 to 95. Users rate the 3000K 95 CRI version's tint very highly (Convoy).

best_for.why_html: Best hotspot-to-spill balance

emitters.name: SFT-60
emitters.notes_html: 5000K/5700K/6500K, 6.0 mm² die, 15 A max. High Vf (~3.3 V @ 10 A, ~3.5 V @ 15 A per one user), so a single-cell buck driver may not reach full current. Sits between SFT-40 and SFT-90 (Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Fatter, higher-lumen hotspot; comes into its own in large reflectors

emitters.name: SFT-42R
emitters.notes_html: Round-die thrower with a bigger hotspot than SFT-40 and ~2 A more draw. Best in large reflectors (Convoy L21B); in TIR or small hosts it throws less than the SFT-40. Phosphor is more brittle than other SFT parts, so don't let a TIR press on it (Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Fatter, higher-lumen hotspot; comes into its own in large reflectors

emitters.name: SFT-90
emitters.notes_html: Much cheaper alternative to the SBT90.2 with slightly lower performance. High Vf at high current makes FET/direct-drive and 1-cell buck drivers a poor match (Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Wall of light and long throw. These big dies are a poor match for 35–40 mm reflectors and need 60 mm+ to peak

best_for.why_html: Enormous output and hotspot; needs a big reflector and a high-current driver

emitters.name: SBT90.2
emitters.notes_html: Monster throw + lumens (~5700K). Expensive and power-hungry (~20 A+), greenish on low modes (BLF Guide, Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Wall of light and long throw. These big dies are a poor match for 35–40 mm reflectors and need 60 mm+ to peak

best_for.why_html: Enormous output and hotspot; needs a big reflector and a high-current driver

emitters.name: SFT-12
emitters.notes_html: About half the SFT-25R's emitting area (6500K). Tight pencil beam, but at the same current the SFT-25R is much brighter and throws further (Convoy).

emitters.name: SST-20
emitters.notes_html: Budget domed emitter. The ≤4000K high-CRI version is R9080; 5000K–6500K is bright but notoriously green on low. Also sold as SST-20-DR 660 nm deep red (Convoy, BLF Guide).

emitters.name: SST-40 / SST-70
emitters.notes_html: Domed, cheap, high-output flood/hybrid LEDs common in budget lights; very green at low power (BLF Guide, Convoy).

emitters.name: XHP70.3 HI
emitters.notes_html: The go-to for high sustained output. Domeless HI (3.9 mm source) roughly doubles intensity and cleans up the beam vs domed HD (5.3 mm source; 4,857 / 6,405 lm) (BLF Guide).

best_for.why_html: High efficiency at high drive means more lumens for the same heat. Sustained output is still set by the host's size and cooling

emitters.name: XHP50.3 HI
emitters.notes_html: Compact quad-die workhorse; very efficient with decent throw, though tint can be a lottery (Convoy).

emitters.name: XHP35.2 HI
emitters.notes_html: Domeless 3535 multi-die. The older 12V XHP35 HI (discontinued) is still sought after for its 4000K tint (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: XP-L HI
emitters.notes_html: Classic domeless EDC emitter; mostly superseded by 519A, SFT-40 and NTG35 (Convoy).

emitters.name: XP-G4 / XP-L2
emitters.notes_html: Efficient and very common in mainstream brands (Fenix, Olight, etc.). Domed, with poor colour and noticeable tint shift; enthusiasts generally avoid them (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: XP-GR / XP-LR / XM-MR / XFLMNR
emitters.notes_html: Cree's newer round-die (round LES) throw parts, with source sizes of 1.3–2.8 mm. Cree's direct answer to the SFT-25R / SFT-40 class. Few enthusiast tests yet.

emitters.name: XHP50.2 / XHP70.2
emitters.notes_html: Older domed XHP generation: very bright but floody, with visible rainbow tint shift. Still sold by Convoy (Convoy Cree).

emitters.name: XFL series
emitters.notes_html: Ultra-high-lumen domed multi-die parts for mega-flooders; mediocre colour.

best_for.why_html: 10,000–20,000 lm class; NV1010 also offered in R9080 (availability varies)

emitters.name: W1
emitters.notes_html: 1 mm² die, cool white (~6000K). Unmatched pencil-beam throw for its size. The same package also comes in red, green, verdure, orange and blue (see §7) (BLF Guide, Convoy Osram).

best_for.why_html: Tiny domeless die = highest luminance of any LED = most candela per lumen

emitters.name: W2
emitters.notes_html: 2 mm² die, 5700K only. Handles more current than W1 for a wider, brighter hotspot (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: Boost HX
emitters.notes_html: 2 mm²-class die in the bigger Oslon Boost package, which runs cooler and takes more overdrive. Common in Convoy throwers (S21B, M21-series) (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: P9
emitters.notes_html: Domed, mainly cool white; competes with the XP-L HD in budget/mainstream lights. Poor colour rendering (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: F45R
emitters.notes_html: 10 A max. 3000K/4000K/5000K. A user described it as "a cross between an SFT40 and an SFT60" (Convoy).

emitters.name: F150R
emitters.notes_html: Rated to 30 A. Convoy says it sits on or below the Planckian locus (no green push). Users report the 4000K as nicely negative-Duv but the 3000K as slightly green. Fits 21700 hosts such as the M21H (Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Wall of light and long throw. These big dies are a poor match for 35–40 mm reflectors and need 60 mm+ to peak

best_for.why_html: Enormous output and hotspot; needs a big reflector and a high-current driver

emitters.name: NV1010
emitters.notes_html: 16 × 75 mil San'an chips; 60–80 A only with excellent cooling. Wide, clean beam; the 5000K R9080 version is praised for neutral tint. Currently listed as unavailable (Convoy).

best_for.why_html: 10,000–20,000 lm class; NV1010 also offered in R9080 (availability varies)

emitters.name: SFN60
emitters.notes_html: Common Emisar / Noctigon hotrod emitter. Decent tint at 6500K, slightly green at 5500K. Competes with the SBT90 on lumens but throws less. May be discontinued; check stock (BLF Guide, Emisar).

emitters.name: Other SF-series
emitters.notes_html: SFQ-55 / SFQ-60 (5050, ~3,000 lm, clean cool tint). SFN-43 (5050, ~4,000 lm). SFN-55.2 (7070, ~8,000 lm, greenish). SFH-43 / SFH-55 (11 × 10 SBT90.2 footprint, 7,000–10,000+ lm). SFP-55 / SFY-55 (11 × 11 / 16 × 16, 20,000+ lm) (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: FFL351A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.notes_html: Domeless flip-chip, ~2 × 2 mm chip, 4.3 mm² glowing area. Beam looks like a dedomed 519A with a slightly larger corona. Efficiency gains flatten above ~5 A. A newer run is reportedly less rosy than early batches. CCTs range from 1800K to 5000K (BLF test). In a 7-emitter light it beat a domed 519A by only ~3% in lumens, with negligible extra throw (1Lumen E07X).

best_for.why_html: High CRI, easy to drive, great tint

emitters.name: FFL505A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.notes_html: Small round die (2.35 mm²) under glass, ringed by brittle white silicone. Same chip as the LMP W5050SQ3, so it's a Lumenpioneer part. Relatively high luminance for a warm high-CRI LED, but very inefficient: 31 lm/W at max, "probably the most inefficient modern 5050" the tester has measured. An SFT-40 3000K matches its throw at ~6 A. A 6500K / 97 CRI version also exists (BLF test, BLF 6500K test).

best_for.why_html: Rosy (FFL) or warm 95 CRI (SFT-40) alternatives to cool-white throwers

emitters.name: FFL707A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.cri_html: "4000K" sample: 4277K, Ra 89, R9 49, Duv −0.016 (claimed −0.001). Another sample: Ra 97–98 (Opple meter)
emitters.notes_html: Four dies in the XHP70.3 HI footprint, but wired differently, so it needs its own board. Less flux and luminance than XHP70.3 HI. The gaps between dies can show a "donut hole" in smooth reflectors. ~9 A is the sensible limit. Samples vary a lot (BLF test).

emitters.name: FFL909A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.footprint_html: 9090 · listed as 3V (36 A max), but a near-identical part tests as ~9V
emitters.notes_html: 36 chips (the tested part was 3S × 12P). Listing claims 100 W, with 5000K Ra70 / 4000K Ra95 / 1800K Ra90 options. Very large emitting area (~71 mm²) means flood only, no throw. Possibly made by Hopthink. The FFL909MX variant (T9R, E90) is reported as brighter but greener (BLF test, BLF T9R).

emitters.name: NTG35
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.lm_html: In a Noctigon D4V2 quad: ~2,900 lm OTF (4200K/5000K), 2,500 (2700K), 2,000 (1800K), Hank's figures. Measured ~2,900 lm turbo in a KR3 triple
emitters.notes_html: Hank's house high-CRI 3535, "free of greenish tint". Maker and construction undisclosed. Users find it rosier than a 219B (sometimes too rosy). Floody beam (~3.8 cd/lm in a KR3 triple). Main rivals: FFL351A, 519A (TG Reviews KR3, Stephen Knight KR3, Noctigon D4V2).

best_for.why_html: High CRI, easy to drive, great tint

emitters.name: NTG50
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.footprint_html: 5050 · 6V (XHP50 footprint and voltage, so a drop-in for 6V XHP50.3 HI). 12V needs a different MCPCB
emitters.lm_html: ~2,100–3,300 lm (no lab test yet). Max ~8 A (listing)
emitters.cri_html: 1800K / 2700K / 4200K / 5000K, ~95 CRI. Hank's charts show Duv ~−0.006 to −0.010
emitters.notes_html: Hank's high-CRI XHP50.3 HI alternative: similar cd/lm, slightly fewer lumens. Hank says a neutral version isn't planned because "we need to guarantee that the tint is on the rosy side". Maker undisclosed (BLF Hank thread).

emitters.name: FFL5009R
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.notes_html: Domeless quad-die "HI" part sold loose in 1800K / 2700K / 4000K / 5000K, plus a rosy 3500K in some lights. The listing gives Duv ±0.0005 for the original 4800–5300K bin. One reviewer reports Ra 95 / R9 97 for the 3500K L50 Sol, with no method stated. It's probably related to the Hopthink FL5009R that koef3 tested (3V, 11.8 mm² glowing area, 3,564 lm @ 20 A at 25 °C, Ra 94, R9 99, Duv −0.002, measured ~5900K). That test found a throwy all-rounder beam, but with a yellowish spot in smooth reflectors (FireflyLite, BLF FL5009R test, BLF L50 Sol review).

emitters.name: FFL5009D
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.notes_html: Domed version of the FFL5009R, with a wider, smoother beam and less throw (170–190 m vs 175–220 m in the same light). 3000K (rosy) / 4000K / 5000K. Only sold in lights (FireflyLite L50 Sol).

emitters.name: FFL350RD
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.notes_html: Sold as a 3500K "round die", but the test found an ordinary rectangular flip chip masked to look round. Measured 4024K with Duv +0.001, not the listed 3500K on-BBL tint. The tester advises staying below 5–6 A: after a few minutes at 8.2 A the part changed (flux up >60%, tint much cooler) and later measured below 90 CRI. Out of stock (FireflyLite, BLF test).

emitters.name: FFL350DD
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.lm_html: ~710–790 lm each (claimed 8,500–9,500 lm from 12 in the E12 Eclipse)
emitters.notes_html: FireflyLite calls it "a big upgrade" on the FFL350RD: a round die with high CRI and better throw. 5700K and 3700K (slightly rosy). Only sold in lights; no test yet (FireflyLite E12 Eclipse Void White).

emitters.name: FFL505HB
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.lm_html: ~1,300 lm each (claimed 5,200 lm from four in the E04 Surge)
emitters.notes_html: Cool white 6000–6500K. Claimed to throw further than the quad FFL505A in the same light (650 m vs 480 m). Only sold in lights (FireflyLite E04 Surge).

emitters.name: FFL707MD
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.notes_html: Round-die high-CRI 7070, 4200K with a slightly rosy tint. Claimed ~480 m in the X1S Pharos reflector version (FireflyLite X1S Pharos RE).

emitters.name: FFL707MX
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.notes_html: 5500K high-output thrower option, claimed at 1,080 m vs 915 m for the SBT90.2 option in the same light. The E90 page also introduces a 9090 round-die FFL909MX and a high-CRI round-die FFL707RD (FireflyLite E90 Blaze).

emitters.name: LHP531
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: 1800K–6500K (1800K is PC-amber style). Very cheap with a clean multi-die beam and slightly rosy 3000K–5000K tint (BLF Test, Convoy).

emitters.name: LHP73B
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: High-power 3V flood/general-purpose competitor to XHP70.3 HI, with higher sustained output in Convoy lights (Convoy, Grzybek).

best_for.why_html: High efficiency at high drive means more lumens for the same heat. Sustained output is still set by the host's size and cooling

emitters.name: W5050SQ3
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: Lumenpioneer's own round-die 3000K thrower (2.3 mm² glowing area). Same chip as the FFL505A, but low-CRI and much more efficient. Higher luminance than the FFL505A and XP-L HI. Lab: 3208K, Duv +0.0015, turning redder as current rises. One Convoy buyer reported ~84 CRI, which the lab didn't reproduce. BLF rates it weaker than the 3000K SFT-40 (BLF test, Convoy).

best_for.why_html: Warm CCT cuts back-scatter glare

emitters.name: W5050SQ5
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: Higher-current round-die thrower (4000K/5000K); tint close to the LHP531 (Convoy).

emitters.name: LML2AW.DC
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: Budget 3000K/4000K drop-in replacement for the SST-40. Users report better tint than the SST-40, though batches vary (Convoy).

emitters.name: GT-FC40
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: 16-die domeless "waffle" emitter (as warm as 1800K). Throws more than a domed XHP70 but has been outcompeted by XHP70.3 HI and FFL707A. Extended-CRI tops at R9050, not R9080 — a correction on the BLF guide thread itself (BLF Guide, Convoy Getian).

emitters.name: NVSU233B(T)
emitters.notes_html: Convoy's premium UV option; clean 365 nm output with minimal visible purple (Convoy Nichia).

emitters.name: SST-10-UV
emitters.notes_html: Budget 365 nm UV. UV LEDs run at a higher Vf (~3.8 V+), so use a UV-rated driver (Convoy Luminus).

emitters.name: SBT-10X-UV
emitters.notes_html: ~1.3–1.4 W radiant @ 1 A (Vf ~3.8–3.9 V), pushed to ~3 A in high-power builds (Convoy).

emitters.name: UVC 255 nm / UVB 310 nm
emitters.notes_html: Specialised Convoy listings. UVC and UVB are hazardous to eyes and skin even at low power. Don't look at the beam, and don't treat UVC as a reliable disinfection tool without a measured dose (Convoy Other LED).

emitters.name: SST-10-IR
emitters.notes_html: Night-vision/covert IR. 850 nm shows a faint red glow; 940 nm is effectively invisible but works less well with most cameras (Convoy Luminus).

emitters.name: Green
emitters.notes_html: Saturated true green; high perceived brightness, popular for hunting and signalling (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: Verdure
emitters.notes_html: Spectrum centred near the eye's 555 nm sensitivity peak, so very high lumens per watt and a distinct "money green" tint (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: Red
emitters.notes_html: Red-orange; protects dark adaptation far better than white. For maximum night-vision preservation, deep red (660 nm, e.g. SST-20-DR) is better (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: Blue
emitters.notes_html: Short-wavelength blue throw emitter (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: Orange
emitters.notes_html: Warm monochrome option, used for wildlife watching and to cut glare in fog and rain (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: GT RGB
emitters.notes_html: RGB emitter on a dedicated board for full-colour setups (Convoy Getian).

emitters.name: XP-E2 (colour)
emitters.notes_html: Long-standing standard for coloured channels in multi-channel builds.

emitters.name: LH351D
emitters.notes_html: Cheap and floody with a big dome; available in cool-white high CRI. Tends green (nicknamed "dogfarts") and bins vary. Superseded by 519A but still a decent budget pick (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: TN3535
emitters.lm_html:
1,050 lm @ 3 A (90 CRI, lab)
~1,970 lm (90 CRI) / ~3,100 lm (70 CRI) at max overdrive (lab, 25 °C)
emitters.notes_html: Domed single-die flip chip, similar to the LH351D. The big 8.4 mm² source makes it a flood LED, not a thrower. The 90 CRI sample measured Ra 94 / R9 71 but had a green tint (Duv +0.0055), and the 70 CRI bins have R9 below −25. Vf goes past 4 V at max current, so avoid direct drive. Found in budget Sofirn and Wurkkos lights (e.g. Sofirn SR23 / ST10, early Wurkkos TS26) (BLF test).

emitters.name: CSP2323
emitters.notes_html: Tiny CSP, brighter than the E21A with slightly worse colour. Popular in small triples such as the Wurkkos TS10 (BLF Guide).

best_for.pick_html: Nichia E21A, 519A or LatticePower CSP2323 in a triple
best_for.why_html: Small, efficient, high CRI at the low currents tiny cells can supply

emitters.name: HL2X
emitters.notes_html: Domed with decent colour; notable 1800K 80 CRI version (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: UHi 20 / UHi 40
emitters.notes_html: Nitecore's in-house emitters (Sysmax). Very high output but very low CRI; found in many current Nitecore lights (BLF Guide).
